obligation: FD&C Act section 524B (cyber devices): Medical Devices
applies: Yes (IX-4, PM-7, US-2 and their related systems; AI-001 when submitted)
basis: Section 524B covers sponsors of 510(k), PMA, PDP, De Novo or HDE submissions for cyber devices. IX-4 (2024), PM-7 and US-2 (2025) were submitted after the section took effect and connect to networks; the AI-001 submission is planned for 2027 Q2. IX-3 was cleared in 2018, before section 524B, and stays under the QMSR, 21 CFR 803 and 806 and FDA postmarket guidance. No size exemption

obligation: FD&C Act section 524B: Distribution, Testing and group
basis: Distribution and Testing submit no device marketing applications; Testing's tests support its clients' submissions

obligation: Quality Management System Regulation: Medical Devices
basis: Medical Devices is a registered device manufacturer with design controls. Distribution does not repackage or relabel (the private-label proposal is on hold), and Testing manufactures no devices

obligation: Medical device reporting: Medical Devices and Distribution
applies: Yes (Medical Devices as manufacturer; Distribution as distributor and as initial importer for 6 product lines)
basis: Manufacturer reports under 803.50 and 803.53; distributor complaint files under 803.18(d); importer event files and reports under 803.18(a) and 803.40. Not applicable to Testing

obligation: Reports of corrections and removals: Medical Devices and Distribution
applies: Yes (Medical Devices as manufacturer; Distribution as initial importer)
basis: 806.10 reports and 806.20 records for the manufacturer; importer corrections for the 6 imported lines; Distribution executes manufacturers' holds

obligation: Establishment registration and device listing: Medical Devices and Distribution
basis: Medical Devices is a registered manufacturer; Distribution is registered as initial importer under 807.20(a)(5)

obligation: FDA premarket (2026) and postmarket (2016) cybersecurity guidance: Medical Devices
applies: Applied as the measure of reasonable assurance (nonbinding)
basis: FDA uses the guidance to judge whether 524B(b)(2) processes give reasonable assurance; IX-3 is managed under the postmarket guidance

obligation: Drug Supply Chain Security Act: Distribution
basis: Distribution distributes no prescription drugs

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Medical Devices (DCC)
basis: The DCC creates, receives, maintains and transmits PHI for about 1,300 hospitals under BAAs, which makes Medical Devices a business associate (45 CFR 160.103) directly subject to the Security Rule. It is not a covered entity; fielded devices store data under hospital control. No size exemption

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Distribution, Testing, DEMS and corporate shared services
applies: No (Distribution, Testing, DEMS); corporate shared services support the DCC through common controls
basis: Distribution holds no PHI except incidental data on returns; Testing prohibits PHI by contract (PHI found in 3 submissions is analyzed as a risk); DEMS holds no PHI

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule business associate provisions: Medical Devices (DCC)
basis: The DCC may use and disclose PHI only as the hospital BAAs permit, including the 24-month rolling retention

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: Medical Devices (DCC)
basis: Notice to each affected hospital under 164.410 and the BAA terms (15 calendar days standard; 5 days for 64 health systems)

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM (2025): all divisions and group
basis: Not a final rule; tracked for planning

obligation: 42 CFR Part 2 (SUD records): all divisions and group
basis: No division operates a federally assisted substance use disorder program

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule: all divisions and group
basis: 16 CFR 318.1 excludes business associates acting as such; the DCC acts as a business associate, and no division offers a consumer health app

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools
applies: No (a duty of hospital customers, not the company)
basis: 45 CFR 92.210 binds covered entities that receive federal financial assistance, such as hospitals that would use AI-001; the company is not one

obligation: CMS emergency preparedness conditions: all divisions and group
basis: No division is a certified provider type

obligation: HIPAA applicability to social assistance: all divisions and group
basis: No division is a social assistance organization

obligation: FAR 52.204-21 basic safeguarding: Distribution
basis: The VA and DoD contracts include the clause, and order, delivery and facility data for about 380 federal facilities are Federal contract information

obligation: FAR 52.204-21 basic safeguarding: Testing and Medical Devices
basis: Neither division holds federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: CMMC Program: Distribution
applies: Yes (Level 1 expected; not yet a term of the contract)
basis: 32 CFR 170.3(c) applies CMMC to DoD contracts under which a contractor processes FCI. The DoD contract (awarded 2024-03, before Phase 1) covers distribution services, so the COTS exception does not apply; DoD may add Level 1 (Self) at the 2027-03-31 option, and Phase 4 (2028-11-10) reaches option periods on earlier contracts

obligation: CMMC Program: Medical Devices
basis: Medical Devices holds no DoD contracts

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012: Distribution
basis: The DoD contract includes the clause, but DoD has marked or provided no covered defense information and Distribution generates none (Group General Counsel decision, 2026-06-30). Recheck at every contract modification

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012: Medical Devices
basis: Medical Devices holds no DoD contracts

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 and CMMC: Testing
basis: Testing holds no federal contracts or subcontracts and no CUI (Group General Counsel decision, 2026-06-30)

obligation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889): Distribution
basis: Both federal contracts include the clause: report covered telecommunications equipment within 1 business day of identification

obligation: ITAR: all divisions and group
basis: No division makes defense articles; no ITAR registration is held

obligation: EAR: all divisions and group
applies: Yes (Medical Devices exports and deemed exports; Testing client technical data; limited for Distribution)
basis: Medical Devices exports to about 40 countries and holds controlled technology in PLM; Testing receives client technical data; group trade compliance classifies items and screens staff

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: all divisions and group
basis: Security and AI claims in marketing of the DCC, Testing services and AI-001 performance

obligation: CTPAT: Distribution
citation: CBP program; SAFE Port Act of 2006 (voluntary)
basis: Distribution imports 6 foreign manufacturers' product lines, but CTPAT is voluntary, no deliverable relies on it, and membership was not reviewed at intake

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure: group
basis: The holding company is an SEC registrant; the FY2025 Form 10-K carries the Item 106 disclosure; divisions contribute incident facts through the group

obligation: CCPA/CPRA and CPPA regulations: group
basis: The group sells to hospitals in all 50 states. DCC data is PHI held as a business associate, which Cal. Civ. Code 1798.146 exempts; no deliverable analyzes employee or business contact data under the CCPA

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Testing and group
basis: The rule covers financial institutions, such as tax preparers; no division is one

obligation: IRC 7216 preparer disclosure rules: Testing
basis: Testing prepares no tax returns

obligation: IRS Publication 4557 WISP expectation: Testing
basis: Testing is not a tax return preparer

obligation: HIPAA as business associate: Testing
applies: No (by design; tracked as a risk)
basis: Client contracts prohibit PHI. Device logs in 3 submissions in 2026 contained patient identifiers, which P03 and P01 analyze as a risk of becoming a subcontractor business associate without agreeing to it

obligation: ABA Model Rules 1.1 and 1.6(c): Testing
citation: ABA Model Rules; Florida Rules 4-1.1 and 4-1.6(e)
basis: Testing provides no legal services

obligation: AICPA Code, confidential client information: Testing
basis: Testing provides no accounting services

obligation: CIRCIA (proposed): all divisions and group
basis: The final rule was not published; tracked for planning

obligation: NIST CSF 2.0 benchmark: Testing
basis: No binding cybersecurity rule applies to Testing, so the division measures itself against CSF 2.0

obligation: State AI employment laws for AI-008 (Colorado SB26-189, Illinois HB 3773, NYC Local Law 144, California ADS regulations): group HR
applies: Yes if AI-008 is deployed (proposed; not approved)
basis: The proposed applicant screening tool would support employment decisions in several states

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification): all divisions
basis: The group holds personal information of Florida residents among its 45,000 employees; the DCC holds data for Florida hospitals as a third-party agent (501.171(6)). Other states' laws apply where affected individuals reside (Florida is the worked example)

obligation: Hospital BAAs: Medical Devices (DCC)
basis: Standard BAA: breach notice within 15 calendar days and security incident reports within 5 business days; 64 health systems negotiated 5-day breach notice

obligation: Testing client NDAs
basis: NDAs with about 950 clients require prompt notice of incidents affecting client information and limit use to the engagement

obligation: ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation: Testing
basis: The accreditation carries confidentiality and impartiality duties for client information

obligation: Supplier and contract manufacturer agreements: Medical Devices
basis: The template requires vulnerability notice and SBOM data from suppliers of software components

obligation: SOC 2 commitments: DCC (existing) and Testing client portal and LIMS (planned)
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; customer contracts
applies: Yes (DCC annually; Testing planned); Distribution out of scope
basis: Hospital customers rely on the annual DCC Type 2 report; 41 Testing clients asked for a report in 2026
